“Corre o risco de mergulhar” is an idiomatic statement of danger, followed by the threatened descent into madness; the shorter arrisca is an optional style change.
“Cada um” is the singular subject of “tem” in an existential proposition asserted by the tale. “Propõe que” presents that proposition, not a wish requiring the subjunctive.
“Food chain” denotes the ecological cadeia alimentar, not the place Corrente.
“Full belly” is a satiated stomach, rendered barriga cheia; it does not identify the location Ventre.
“Warning” describes the Kojin warning their children, rendered avisando; it does not identify an entity named Aviso.
In “É bem sabido que”, bem modifies the participle sabido in a verbal predicate. It is not the compound attributive adjective bem-sabido.
“Gathering around floating bodies” is the fish’s habit of clustering, rendered se reunir ao redor de corpos flutuantes; it does not name Assembleia.
“Runs the migratory gauntlet” metaphorically describes the crab’s demanding river migration, rendered maratona migratória; it does not name Corredor de Provações.
“Extremo Oriente” is the proper geographical name Far East, not a lower-case cardinal direction.
“Como é o caso deste crustáceo” introduces the fish as an example of spontaneous naming; the full idiom is grammatical and preserves the narrator’s explanatory aside.
“The first thing” is the first nearby object seen by the discoverer, rendered primeira coisa; it does not identify the world Primeiro.
“Do lates” is a singular possessive complement of plural “os olhos”: both eyes belong to one fish. The following verb ficaram agrees with olhos.
The Portuguese cobra/cobras renders generic snake/snakes in all four versions of the fish-origin legend. No source identifies the naja species named by BNpc Cobra.
“Trained/untrained eye” means expert or lay perception of shell anatomy, rendered olhar treinado/leigo; it does not name Olho.
“Hot water” sets up the cooking-cauldron joke, rendered água quente; it does not identify the location Águas Quentes.
“Um grande avanço” characterizes the academics’ claimed breakthrough and supports the contrast with the unimpressed Kojin; grande is meaningful emphasis.
“Certamente” precedes “desaparece” to assert the certainty of the fish disappearing at dinner. This adverb position is grammatical and preserves the joke.
“Shade of rocks” is shelter from daylight, rendered sombra das rochas; it is not the enemy Vulto.
“Depois de serem arrastados” is a grammatical temporal infinitive clause explaining when the shrimp fell from the sky; após is only a stylistic alternative.
“Sea scholar” is the marine researcher for whom the shark was named, rendered estudioso dos mares; it does not name Erudito.
“Bubble eye” names the Doman fish’s inflated eye feature, rendered olhos-de-bolha. Eye is not the place Olho.
“Muito mais provável” compares encountering the shell on Ala Mhigan tables with finding a live specimen in Loch Seld; the comparative has an explicit basis.
“Shade of pink” is the fish’s color, rendered tom de rosa; it is not the enemy Vulto.
“Sphere of dominion” is the young fish’s perceived territory, rendered domínio; it does not name Dominion.
“The first time, and every time” emphasizes the fish’s consistent flavor, adapted as da primeira à última garfada; it does not name the world Primeiro.
“Imposing frame” means the fish’s physique, rendered porte imponente; it does not name Estrutura.
“Phenomenon” is the astronomical eclipse, rendered fenômeno astronômico; “the scales” are fish escamas. Neither names Phenomenon or Balança.
“Cobra” is Portuguese for a generic snake: the source English snake and the other three sources do not identify the naja species or BNpc Cobra.
“Food chain” is the ecological cadeia alimentar of Loch Seld; chain does not identify the place Corrente.
“Held dominion over Lakeland” is the elves’ historical rule, rendered domina a Terra dos Lagos; it is not the BNpc Dominion.
“Nascente” is the current proper name of the lake The Source in Lakeland, reinforced by the lake setting in all four sources.
“Shade gudgeon” is this fish’s descriptive name, rendered gobiões-sombra. It does not refer to the separate enemy Shade/Vulto.
“Purple pods” are the mucus-and-mud cocoons, rendered casulos roxos; they are not Pod machines.
“The shallow pools” are generic shallow fish habitat, rendered poças rasas; they do not name Camada Rasa.
“Uns aos outros” marks reciprocal recognition among the fish using their individual light patterns; the reciprocal construction is grammatical.
“Anglers” denotes people who see and catch these luminous fish, rendered pescadores; it is not the fish enemy Peixe-pescador.
“Source of food” is an ordinary supply of nourishment, rendered fonte de alimento; it does not name either the lake Nascente or the world Origem.
“Shade” describes the fish’s attractive coloration, rendered cor; it is not the creature Vulto.
“Faces” denotes the fish’s doubtful facial expression, rendered cara bem mais desconfiada; it does not name enemy Rostos.
“Golden fringes” are the borders of fish fins, rendered bordas douradas; they do not name the region Fronteiras.
“Em grande parte” qualifies how much regeneration contributed to survival, leaving room for other causes as in English “in no small part”.
“Vista” is the imperative of vestir in the instruction Vista roupas discretas; it does not name the place Mirante.
“Depois de escolher um rumo” is a temporal infinitive clause before the main verb recusa-se. The full expression is grammatical.
“Cliff faces” are the vertical underwater rock walls, rendered paredões submersos; faces does not refer to human or enemy Rostos.
“Shaft-like body” compares the fish to an arrow shaft, rendered corpo esguio como uma haste; it does not name a Poço.
“Wanderer” denotes a generic traveler seeing a hallucinatory fish, rendered viajante; it is not an enemy named Andarilho.
“Riverbed rubble” is natural stone cover, rendered cascalhos; it does not name animated Entulho enemies.
“Oyster hunters” denotes people seeking edible shellfish, rendered caçadores de ostras; it does not identify the female enemy named caçadora de ostras.
“A maior parte do tempo” quantifies the duration the fish remains buried, matching English “most of its time”; it is not a redundant phrase.
“A flurry of darting teeth” is the rapid attack of the fish’s teeth, rendered saraivada de dentes velozes; it does not name the location Nevasca.
“Children of the Storm” is the fish’s fae epithet, rendered Filhos da Tempestade; “lightning bolts” are the claimed origin as raios. Neither identifies the BNpc Tempestade or Lightning.
“Dominion” denotes this fish’s social dominance over its kin, rendered dominar; it is not the BNpc named Dominion.
“Tear” is the action of ripping fish scales, rendered rasgar; it does not name the enemy Lágrima.
“The scales” are fish scales, rendered escamas; they do not identify the place Balança.
“Nascente” names the lake The Source, whose peoples transmit Bismarck’s legend; it is not a cardinal direction.
“Unknown” qualifies the purpose of the fish’s horn, rendered desconhecida; it does not identify an enemy called Desconhecido.
The alternatives are the complete groups “duas cores ou menos” and “quatro cores ou mais”. The comma separates those two excluded ranges, not the internal lower-bound ou.
“The emperor’s dominion over all” is imperial authority symbolized by the fish tribute, rendered domínio do imperador sobre tudo; it is not Dominion.
“Agora” is the Portuguese temporal adverb in the fish’s new feeding behavior; it does not name an Ágora location.
“Em grande parte” allows limited nonornamental use of the scale armor, matching the qualified English “largely”; removing it would make the restriction absolute.
“Provavelmente” modifies the whole predicate “está relacionado à sua posição”. The adverb may precede this predicate without changing the singular subject tamanho.
“A neve vermelha de sangue” compares the shine with snow used generically, without a definite article. Semelhante supplies the preposition a, so no article contraction is required.
“Fácil” is the predicate of the infinitive “avistar este tubarão”, not an adjective modifying plural escamas; its singular form is correct.
“Calor escaldante” describes the extreme geothermal heat that hardens the dorsal spines. The vivid description is appropriate to this creature entry.
“Barbs” are the fish’s mineral dorsal spines, rendered espinhos minerais; “the deep waters” is generic águas profundas. Neither names Farpas or Profundezas.
“Pods” are the fish’s small swimming groups, rendered pequenos cardumes; they are not Pod machines.
“Shades” denotes the fish’s attractive colors, rendered cores belas e vivas; it does not name Vultos.
“A cor vermelha característica” is the subject whose cause is explained by the following calcário clause; the reference to color is clear and grammatical.
“Deep-sea” locates the serpentiform fish in deep marine water, rendered mares profundos; it does not identify the place Profundezas.
“Pode ser vista atraindo” is the passive observation of the fish at the bazaar; vista does not name Mirante.
“Face” is the verb confront in the fish’s defensive behavior, rendered enfrentá-lo; it does not name enemy Rosto.
“Number” counts the many tetras in the Font of Maya, rendered quantidade de tetras, as evidence for the reincarnation joke; it is not the BNpc Número.
“The beholder” is whoever judges the fish’s eye-like markings, rendered quem o observa; it does not name the enemy Observador.
“Mimic” is the verb for the small crabs’ camouflage as pebbles, rendered imitam; it is not a mimic monster.
“Mimic” is the verb for imitating the movement of seaweed, rendered imitar; it is not a mimic monster.
“A maior parte da vida” quantifies the time this poor swimmer spends attached to rocks, matching English “most of its life”.
“Deep” describes an intense blue coloration, rendered azul profundo; it does not identify Profundezas.
“The depths of the lochs” describes deep salt-lake water, rendered águas profundas dos lagos salgados; it is not a named Profundezas location.
“Boulders” are lakebed stones imitated by the fish, rendered pedras. “Mimic” is the verb imitar that describes camouflage, not the creature Mímico.
“Observer” is the person whose eyes perceive the panther comparison, rendered alguém; it does not identify an enemy Observador.
“Deep below the surface” describes little light at depth, rendered nas profundezas; “vista” is ordinary Portuguese sight in visão ruim. Neither phrase names Profundeza Inferior or Mirante.
“Enemy katana” are the opposing warriors’ weapons, rendered katanas inimigas; enemy does not name the place Inimigo.
“Proof” belongs to the ordinary idiom putting a theory to the test, rendered à prova: Sharlayan cooking tests whether shell-inlaid dishes improve flavor. It does not identify Testemunho.

“Grande quantidade de calor corporal” expresses the copious heat that permits survival in freezing water; grande supplies the source’s degree. “Mesmo depois de limpa e eviscerada” gives the time condition under which the fish flesh remains warm. Depois de is a valid temporal construction.
“The scales” are fish escamas; “deep” describes dark olive green, and “the darker hue” is tonalidade mais escura. These phrases do not identify Balança, Profundezas or Trevas Profundas.
“Progenitor” describes a remote ancestor of this fish associated with Karvarhur, rendered ancestral; it does not identify the BNpc Progenitor.
“Wing of Reflection”, rendered Ala da Reflexão, is the named Sharlayan institution studying the fish. Reflection is not the enemy Reflexo.
“First” refers to when this species arose, rendered surgiu; it does not identify the world Primeiro.
The subject of “é testemunhar” is the whole infinitive clause beginning “Observar um cardume”. “Os juncos cintilantes” is the object inside that clause, not the subject of é.
“Tail fin” is the anatomical nadadeira caudal of a freshwater fish; it does not identify a detached enemy named Cauda.
“Plentiful numbers” means the fish are abundant, rendered abundância; it is not the BNpc Número.
“Sent to a watery grave” is an idiom for drowning, rendered encontraram a morte por afogamento; it does not name the enemy Túmulo Aquático.
“Observer” is whoever sees the fish’s apparent legs, rendered quem olha; it does not name Observador.
“Deep blue” is the dark blue color of the caldera water, rendered azul-escuras; it does not identify the character Azul Profundo.
“Deep blue waters” describes the caldera water’s dark blue color, rendered águas azul-escuras; it does not name Profundezas.
“Vista” is in the passive “é vista se deslocando”, describing observed turtle movements; it does not name Mirante.
“Approach” is the verb of nearing a crocodile, rendered aproximar-se; it does not identify Acesso.
“Number” refers to how often the fish flops, rendered quantas vezes; it is an ordinary count, not the enemy Número.
